# Authored browser source

This directory contains authored source and checked-in third-party bundles. Read the [repository map](../docs/repository-map.md) and [feature docs](../docs/README.md) before changing a surface. Do not regenerate, move or delete `dist/` as if it were a build output. [vendor](vendor/) has separate provenance; `downloads/` is generated and may be absent in a fresh checkout.

[index.html](index.html) controls deferred-script dependencies and stylesheet cascade order. Most scripts share globals, DOM IDs and custom events rather than imports. Search existing callers/selectors with `rg` before adding a global or ID. Keep model validation separate from DOM effects where the feature already does so. Refresh a changed asset's content-hash query in the HTML and run [asset-cache checks](../scripts/check-asset-cache.mjs). Preserve intentional API namespaces such as repository preview versus GitHub monitor.

The main state owner is [app.js](app.js); [window.js](window.js) snapshots/transfers workspace state. Preserve saved keys, conversation/pane identities and in-progress input across render, docking and resize. Trace shell input ownership through [shell-input.js](shell-input.js) and [terminal.js](terminal.js); a host-level capture editor must not turn terminal input into a provider prompt. [escape.js](escape.js) is the final dismissal fallback after local dialogs and menus.

Use [bridge.js](bridge.js) for approved native operations, paired with the native receiver. External embeds have a separate trust boundary. [vnc-client.js](vnc-client.js) imports the pinned noVNC runtime and uses a native token-bound TCP adapter or the selected secure WebSocket gateway; keep its session/credential retirement separate from iframe viewers. Do not enable the legacy development-WebSocket fallback or bypass sign-in to obtain a preview. [The isolated layout fixture](../scripts/fixtures/widget-fit.html) supplies synthetic host responses without real tools. `npm run dev` intentionally serves sign-in/downloads, not the machine-backed workspace.

Package text must render as text; remote content uses the existing sanitization/URL policies. Do not add executable content, raw native methods or credentials to [tool definitions](tools/). Follow [tool authoring](../docs/tools.md) for packages and [the shared model](tools-model.js) for validation. New UI controls require keyboard/Escape/focus behavior and stale-result retirement consistent with their host lifecycle. Run the matching [checks](../scripts/) and `npm run check`; distinguish fixture screenshots from installed native acceptance.

New tool packages require schemaVersion 2 and page; legacy v1 definitions stay compatible in Widgets. [page-widgets.js](page-widgets.js) owns page tab adapters and inline renderer disposal, while [application-chrome.js](application-chrome.js) owns the freely resizable application header. Keep existing native panes mounted and retire inactive tool reads without recreating timers, PTYs or chat sessions. See [the page/window contract](../docs/widget-pages-and-application.md).

The checked-in create-markdown runtime comes from the [vendored tokenizer](../vendor-src/create-markdown/packages/core/src/parsers/tokenizer.ts) and [builder](../scripts/build-markdown.mjs). Preserve its local linear-prefix security patch, rebuild after source changes, refresh the loader hash and run [the source/runtime ReDoS and parity check](../scripts/check-markdown-redos.mjs) before delivery.

[widget-lifecycle.js](widget-lifecycle.js) owns built-in installation independently of account connection; imported activation stays on tool instances. Gate callable operations and retire pending responses when deactivated, preserve user content and legacy installation migration, and keep Widgets management available. See [optional widgets](../docs/widget-lifecycle.md) and [lifecycle checks](../scripts/check-widget-lifecycle.mjs).

[spotify-library.js](spotify-library.js) browses read-only account pages through [music-auth.js](music-auth.js). Native library requests return normalized songs/playlists without tokens; retire results on disconnect, expiry, account/service change and widget deactivation. Select items through the existing music source form so playback and account access keep their separate provider sessions.

[Task Manager](../docs/task-manager.md) uses [task-manager-store.js](task-manager-store.js) to share Projects items and lists. Preserve existing task IDs, detail text and workflow/archive semantics. Only successful shared item saves emit `open-sesame-items-changed`. [task-manager.js](task-manager.js) owns the draft, filters and completion UI; [window.js](window.js) carries its in-memory draft during handoff. Do not create a parallel task database or allow inactive widget mutations.

[lockin.js](lockin.js) owns local-media play/seek; [media-transport.js](media-transport.js) adds shared volume, fullscreen and empty/drag hints to the same bar and video element; native controls are reserved for fullscreen. Keep live/unknown-duration seek disabled and preserve queue/file ownership in [lockin.js](lockin.js). Process presentation disclosures in [agent-monitor.js](agent-monitor.js) must preserve identity-bound native controls and explicit stop confirmation.

[Image Studio](../docs/image-generation.md) uses the optional installation lifecycle and Media page adapter. Only explicit Generate sends a prompt; retire pending requests when hidden, deactivated or transferred. Keep prompt/shape drafts local and preview pixels out of shared workspace snapshots. Provider sign-in and export remain native operations.

[mobile-shell.js](mobile-shell.js) owns responsive presentation over mounted panes; [mobile-model.js](mobile-model.js) derives Today from existing state. Keep native macOS modes excluded and preserve saved activity keys, capture ownership and page-widget identities. See the [mobile contract](../docs/mobile-shell.md); reference typography/mark and device qualification remain separate gates.

Narrow mobile Projects uses the existing `libraryOpen` flag and [Projects owner](projects-overview.js) `closeDetails()` transition for collection/detail navigation. Keep save veto and focus return intact; do not add parallel item selection or persistence state in the mobile shell.

Mobile Today task actions and Reader links call canonical owners. Familiar initial seals derive only from canonical IDs/display names, preserve custom avatar images and are decorative, never presence or permission. Keep the projection model loaded before familiar rendering; mobile CSS/roster orientation must restore desktop behavior when its scope ends.

Mobile Task Manager keeps its form and task list in the installed page view’s scrolling flow, so enlarged controls cannot collapse the list. Preserve the native desktop list layout and the page scroll anchor during destination changes.

Mobile Calendar and Reader styling retains their existing data, scheduling, pagination and article-scroll owners. Tools restores focus on dialog close, after native modal dismissal; an explicit installed-page route suppresses that restoration. Keep viewport-only presentation scoped to the mobile shell.

[content-focus.js](content-focus.js) changes presentation without remounting live content; [escape.js](escape.js) restores focused content before collapsing the app and ignores retargeted keyup events. [rail-headings.js](rail-headings.js) delegates full-row targets to existing rail controls while preserving nested actions. [terminal-clipboard.js](terminal-clipboard.js) owns terminal selection/context-menu shortcuts and retires late paste reads after destination changes. [workspace-widgets.js](workspace-widgets.js) gates native view/navigation visibility with lifecycle state while [familiar-capture.js](familiar-capture.js) and [familiar-routing-model.js](familiar-routing-model.js) prepare default or explicitly tagged familiar drafts without sending them.

Today task edits and completion must use Task Manager and its lifecycle-guarded shared store. Inactive content routes to the available Widgets entry without activation. Preserve the content-focus Escape-before-Today order and explicit fresh-profile widget defaults.

[speaker-model.js](speaker-model.js) aligns bounded native word timestamps to anonymous model intervals; overlap and unattributed text remain explicit. [speaker-transcript.js](speaker-transcript.js) owns opt-in setup, names, display and export, preserving the plain transcript when attribution is unavailable. [media-popout.js](media-popout.js) uses native video PiP or isolated provider windows; it never grants an external player the app bridge.

[design-tokens.css](design-tokens.css) is the only place a color, text size, radius, duration or shadow value is written; it loads first. Use its semantic tokens, keep text at or above `--text-caption`, and edit the rule that owns a declaration instead of adding a later override sheet. Do not anchor `:has()` on `html`, `body`, `#widget-anchor` or `#widget-panel`: set a state class on the root from [app.js](app.js) `render()` or the owning module. Write root classes and inherited custom properties once per render with their settled value, and use `closest('[hidden]')` to skip layout work for a hidden surface. Follow [the design system contract](../docs/design-system.md): capture the [rendered baseline](../scripts/review-design-baseline.mjs) before a visual change, compare after it, and keep the [cascade budget](../scripts/check-design-budget.mjs) and [switch-cost budget](../scripts/review-switch-cost.mjs) holding. Shared controls are primitives in [flat-theme.css](flat-theme.css): every horizontal `[role=tablist]` is one segmented tab strip, so a surface may place a strip but must not restate its height, padding, border, radius, color or states; control heights come from `--control-xs` to `--control-lg`; a text input, textarea or select takes its surface, line, radius and focus line from the field rule in the theme, a search box is a `ui-field-group` wrapper with a bare input inside it, and new wrappers join those rules instead of restating them; and a button takes its surface, line, ink, radius and states from the quiet, secondary, primary or accent rule in the theme (`ui-button-quiet`, `ui-button`, `ui-button-primary`, `ui-button-accent` for new markup; `ui-row`, `ui-panel`, `ui-card` and `ui-popover` for rows, panels, cards and popovers), with its own stylesheet setting only size and placement and a button-specific state setting `--button-ink`, `--button-fill` or `--button-line`. Elements whose ids appear in [the recorded nesting facts](../scripts/design-ancestry.json) must stay inside the listed ancestor. [mobile-shell.css](mobile-shell.css) keeps reference-exact values and [sign-in.css](sign-in.css) migrates under its own review; both are held out of the token codemod. Any page that links a tokenized stylesheet, including [sign-in.html](sign-in.html), must link the token sheet first.
